evan: heads-up — ran a across-GPU token-shape sweep (A10/T4/L4/A100/H100). L4 shows a reproducible p99 regression (~+12%) when max_tokens_per_batch >= 4096 under steady qps=220. :thinking:
maria: do you have the profiler counters / kernel mix?
evan: paste below (summary across same prompt mix, 2048 seq avg):
```
-- A100: matmul 72% | kv_lookup 6% | memcpy 12% | kernel_fallback 10% | p99=38ms
-- H100: matmul 74% | kv_lookup 5% | memcpy 10% | kernel_fallback 11% | p99=34ms
-- A10:  matmul 61% | kv_lookup 12%| memcpy 14% | kernel_fallback 13% | p99=46ms
-- T4:   matmul 55% | kv_lookup 15%| memcpy 13% | kernel_fallback 17% | p99=62ms
-- L4:   matmul 48% | kv_lookup 22%| memcpy 14% | kernel_fallback 16% | p99=74ms
```
evan: notable: L4 has higher kv_lookup fraction and kernel_fallback rate. That aligns with observed p99.
jon: is this the continuous-batching heuristic only changing max_tokens_per_batch or are we also changing queue ordering?
evan: only max_tokens_per_batch + a small tweak to token_budget_target in this sweep (0.8 -> 0.9). Queue policy remained weighted_headway.
arjun: possible root causes: 1) L4's kernel for KV gather degenerates at large composite batch sizes, 2) L2/warning eviction pressure causing more KV cache misses, 3) our kernel selection fallback triggers a slower path when total tokens exceed threshold.
sophia: can you dump a small kernel selection log for an L4 case where fallback happened?
evan: yes, snippet from runtime logs (trimmed):
```
[2026-02-22T13:12:04Z] request_batch id=0x7f3 size=28 requests total_tokens=112640 gpu=L4
[2026-02-22T13:12:04Z] kernel_picker: chosen=fast_matmul_v2, expected_seq=2048, workspace=1.2GB
[2026-02-22T13:12:04Z] kernel_picker: fallback_triggered -> kv_kernel_generic (reason=workspace_overflow)
[2026-02-22T13:12:04Z] kv_cache: hits=0.62, misses=0.38, retention_ratio=0.47
```
evan: retention_ratio under load is low on L4 (0.47) vs A100 (0.82). That explains more KV work and memcopies.
maria: what's the current per-GPU max_tokens_per_batch map used in the sweep?
evan: current sweep config (yaml):
```
continuous_batching:
  max_tokens_per_batch:
    default: 4096
    per_gpu:
      A100: "16384"
      H100: "24576"
      A10: "8192"
      T4:  "6144"
      L4:  "4096"
  queue_policy: "weighted_headway"  # alpha=0.7
  token_budget_target: "0.90"
```
maria: so L4 at 4096 is already the problematic point. Try lowering to 3072 or 2560 to see KV retention improve and fallback reduce.
evan: I ran 3072 quick canary: p99 drops from 74ms -> 61ms, kv retention up 0.47 -> 0.62, kernel_fallback down 16% -> 9%. Good sign.
jon: can we implement an adaptive cap: compute rolling kv_retention and if <0.6 then cap max_tokens_per_batch = floor(current / 1.33) for that GPU? That avoids fixed thresholds across different prompt mixes.
arjun: caution: adaptive cap may oscillate under bursty load. We should add hysteresis and min dwell time (e.g., 5min) and queue_policy awareness.
sophia: proposed heuristic POC (pseudocode):
```
- measure kv_retention over 1m window
- if kv_retention < 0.6 and kernel_fallback_rate > 0.08:
    new_max = max(floor(max_tokens_per_batch * 0.75), min_tokens)
    apply with 5m cooldown
- else slowly ramp up by +10% every 10m until default cap
```
evan: I like that. Also suggest adding a per-GPU token-budget target multiplier (tb_mult) because same token_budget_target underweights cache pressure differences. Example tweaks: A100 tb_mult=1.0, H100=1.0, A10=0.95, T4=0.9, L4=0.85.
maria: action items: 1) evan - wire the kv_retention metric into continuous-batching controller (PR), 2) jon - add hysteresis + cooldown logic, 3) arjun - run an overnight sweep with adaptive heuristic on staging (A10/T4/L4 nodes), 4) perf-bot - add alert when per-gpu p99 increases >10% after config rollout.
perf-bot: noted. New alert rule will be created: "batching.max_tokens.p99_regression" with threshold=+10% over baseline 30m.
evan: I'm going to push a small canary rollout to 5% of production for L4 with max_tokens=3072 + tb_mult=0.85. Will monitor KV retention and kernel_fallback. :eyes: 
maria: keep an eye on end-to-end throughput; lowering max_tokens can raise cost if it increases per-token overhead. We need cost/latency tradeoff dashboard for each GPU type.
evan: agreed — I'll capture token-cost delta in the sweep and post summary tomorrow.
sophia: small doc note: add per-gpu recommended defaults in infra config (so new clusters pick conservative L4 defaults).
evan: sounds good. I'll update infra defaults + open PR for adaptive heuristic.
arjun: fyi, we should also file an upstream issue for the L4 kv_kernel so kernel authors can optimize the gather path.
evan: created task #INF-1229: "Investigate L4 KV gather perf and reduce fallback"
maria: thanks — marking this thread resolved for now, we'll reconvene after overnight sweep. :white_check_mark:
